pitches.A: Dead Circuit reimagines EEE labs as timed escape-room challenges designed to combat the biggest crisis in engineering education: students who show up but switch off. Teams are dropped into broken systems with one job: find the fault, fix it, escape.
pitches.B: Engineering students are disengaging at alarming rates. Dead Circuit answers with escape-room-style lab scenarios where teams diagnose realistically broken systems under timed pressure using probe-measure-hypothesis-repair loops.
pitches.C: Students do not need more slides. They need stakes. Dead Circuit transforms EEE labs into timed escape rooms where teams repair broken electrical systems before the clock hits zero.

scenarios.title: Campus Subpanel Blackout
scenarios.brief: A teaching wing has lost low-voltage distribution. Restore a DC feeder board before backup power drains.
preTaskBrief: Safety first: verify isolation and confirm test instrument setup before touching the panel.
Focus points under time pressure: protection path, continuity path, and divider midpoint voltage.
Record one sentence per action: test performed, reading observed, and what it means.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: explain how a wrong divider value could mislead a downstream control input and propose a preventive maintenance check.
objectives: Correct resistor substitution in divider branch

teaching.vocationalScenario: You are maintenance technicians assigned to a college workshop where a low-voltage teaching bench has failed before practical assessments. Learners must apply safe fault-finding procedure, accurate measurement, and documented repair decisions.
lectureSegment: Introduce safe isolation, proving dead, and visual inspection sequence.
Recap series/parallel voltage drops and protective device function.
Model a structured fault log: symptom, test, inference, action.
activitySegment: Teams inspect board, log first observations, and assign technician roles.
Learners probe nodes, compare measured values to expected values, and shortlist faults.
Teams execute repair plan, re-test, and present maintenance justification.
pass: Follow a safe process and identify at least one correct fault.
Use basic measurements and complete a simple fault report.
merit: Independently identify both core faults using measurement evidence.
Justify component replacement choices against circuit behaviour.
Demonstrate effective team communication and role allocation.
distinction: Diagnose and repair faults efficiently with minimal unnecessary actions.
Evaluate alternative hypotheses and reject them using data.
Produce professional maintenance documentation suitable for handover.

components.name: Fuse F1
components.clue: Visual inspection: fuse element is open.

components.name: Resistor R2
components.clue: Band code does not match schematic value.

components.name: Supply V1
components.clue: Output reads nominal under no-load test.

components.name: Load L1
components.clue: Load resistance measured in expected range.

scenarios.debrief: Protection and divider accuracy were both compromised. Correcting both restored regulated distribution.

scenarios.title: Conveyor Motor Driver Lockout
scenarios.brief: A conveyor motor refuses to start during an automated packing assessment. Driver board reports gate activity but no rotation.
preTaskBrief: Set a diagnostic sequence before action: diode orientation -> gate continuity -> current path.
Ignore non-critical noise; capture only readings that confirm or reject a fault hypothesis.
Assign one learner as safety checker to challenge unsafe shortcut decisions.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: relate gate floating behavior to switching losses and discuss how this might impact thermal stress over repeated cycles.

teaching.vocationalScenario: You are called to an industrial learning cell where a conveyor driver has failed mid-production simulation. Learners must apply maintenance troubleshooting under time pressure while maintaining safe procedure and traceability.
lectureSegment: Review motor driver architecture and flyback protection purpose.
Explain gate-drive path, continuity checks, and safe test points.
Discuss maintenance risk of unsafe temporary shortcuts.
activitySegment: Teams map likely fault domains before touching hardware.
Learners collect electrical evidence at gate, drain, and current nodes.
Teams propose and execute a repair sequence, then verify safe restart.
pass: Identify one likely control-path fault and one safe corrective action.
Use continuity and voltage tests appropriately.
merit: Identify both faults with evidence-linked reasoning.
Carry out a safe and ordered repair process with minimal tutor input.
Explain why unsafe alternatives are rejected.
distinction: Deliver a rapid, accurate diagnosis with clean re-commissioning checks.
Correlate measurements to switching behaviour and protection design.
Present a professional technical debrief with preventive recommendations.

components.name: Flyback Diode D1
components.clue: Stripe orientation is opposite to schematic direction.

components.name: Gate Trace
components.clue: Continuity test fails between driver IC and MOSFET gate.

components.name: MOSFET Q1
components.clue: Static diode mode test passes.

components.name: Motor Coil
components.clue: Winding resistance is nominal.

scenarios.debrief: Protection orientation and gate continuity were both blockers. Driver output became valid only after both fixes.

scenarios.title: Audio Amplifier Distortion Emergency
scenarios.brief: A lab demo amplifier overheats and clips badly. Recover stable bias and signal swing before the public showcase.
preTaskBrief: Start with a bias plan: identify expected DC operating points before replacing parts.
Prioritise mission-critical nodes: collector, emitter, and output distortion indicator.
Use a team callout routine: read value, compare baseline, agree implication before action.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: estimate how each fault contributes to THD increase and propose a post-repair verification checklist for quality assurance.

teaching.vocationalScenario: You are advanced maintenance trainees preparing a public engineering showcase rig. The amplifier chain fails thermal and quality checks. Learners must deliver high-standard diagnosis, repair, and technical reporting.
lectureSegment: Explain transistor bias stability and thermal runaway indicators.
Review emitter degeneration and linearity in service contexts.
Discuss capacitor polarity failures and quality assurance checks.
activitySegment: Teams analyse distorted waveform symptoms and assign test strategy.
Learners capture key bias and distortion readings, then triage fault causes.
Teams apply full repair, validate performance restoration, and defend decisions.
pass: Identify at least two relevant faults using guided measurements.
Apply basic corrective actions with supervision.
Record final operating state after repair.
merit: Diagnose all key faults and implement a coherent repair plan.
Demonstrate accurate interpretation of bias and distortion evidence.
Produce structured notes linking fault causes to outcomes.
distinction: Deliver precise and efficient full restoration with robust verification.
Evaluate circuit behaviour at system level and predict reliability impact.
Present an industry-style maintenance report with future mitigation actions.

components.name: Bias Pot RBias
components.clue: Wiper is set far beyond target quiescent point.

components.name: Emitter Resistor RE
components.clue: Open-circuit reading detected.

components.name: Input Coupling Capacitor Cin
components.clue: Electrolytic polarity reversed relative to DC bias.

components.name: Speaker Load
components.clue: Impedance sweep is healthy.

repairOptions.label: Reset RBias to target idle current

scenarios.debrief: Bias, emitter stabilization, and coupling direction all impacted linear operation. Closing all three faults restored headroom and thermal stability.

scenarios.title: Tank Level PLC False Alarm
scenarios.brief: A process training skid keeps tripping high-level alarms even when the tank is half full. Restore stable sensor input for the PLC.
preTaskBrief: Identify signal chain order first: sensor output -> conditioning stage -> PLC analog input.
Focus on one variable at a time; avoid changing both hardware and software simultaneously.
Record expected voltage/current range before probing live nodes.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: propose a calibration and maintenance schedule that would prevent repeat false alarms.
objectives: Verify sensor supply and return integrity

teaching.vocationalScenario: Learners are maintenance technicians on a process-control training rig. They must resolve unstable instrumentation while preserving safe troubleshooting protocol and diagnostic traceability.
lectureSegment: Review instrumentation loops and analog signal standards used in process systems.
Explain offset errors and how they appear at PLC input channels.
Discuss maintenance documentation for calibration-critical systems.
activitySegment: Teams map the complete sensor-to-PLC chain before testing.
Learners capture measurements at each stage and isolate the fault domain.
Teams apply correction and verify stable alarm behavior under simulation.
pass: Follow a safe test sequence and identify one correct fault contributor.
Use measurements to compare expected and actual signal values.
Return system to operational status with tutor support.
merit: Accurately diagnose both faults and justify corrective actions.
Demonstrate clear signal-chain reasoning during troubleshooting.
distinction: Restore system quickly with minimal unnecessary interventions.
Critically evaluate other possible fault causes using evidence.
Produce a professional maintenance recommendation including calibration control.

components.name: Level Sensor S1
components.clue: Output drifts upward at rest despite stable tank level.

components.name: Pull-up Resistor RPU
components.clue: Measured value is significantly lower than design target.

components.name: PLC AI0 Channel
components.clue: Input module self-test passes.

components.name: 24V Instrument Supply
components.clue: Supply remains within tolerance under load.

repairOptions.label: Replace pull-up resistor to design value

scenarios.debrief: Both sensor drift and conditioning bias error contributed to false alarms. Correcting both restored stable process signaling.

scenarios.title: Three-Phase Pump Starter Trip
scenarios.brief: A workshop pump starter drops out seconds after energizing. Restore reliable start-up while preserving protective coordination.
preTaskBrief: Confirm lockout/tagout and verify all three phases before control testing.
Separate power faults from control faults in your test sequence.
Do not bypass protection as a permanent fix.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: explain how nuisance tripping differs from protective coordination failure and suggest commissioning checks.
objectives: Verify contactor coil health and hold circuit

teaching.vocationalScenario: Learners act as industrial maintenance technicians responding to repeated starter trips in a simulated plant environment.
lectureSegment: Review three-phase starter circuits and overload relay functions.
Explain control hold-in logic and contactor failure modes.
Discuss safe re-commissioning checks in rotating machinery systems.
activitySegment: Teams build a starter troubleshooting flowchart before probing.
Learners validate supply, overload, and contactor subsystems with evidence.
Teams perform repair and confirm stable starter operation over repeated cycles.
pass: Identify at least two relevant faults using guided checks.
Apply safe repair actions under supervision.
merit: Diagnose all major faults with evidence-based logic.
Demonstrate effective sequencing between control and power checks.
Provide clear justification for protection settings.
distinction: Restore stable operation efficiently while preserving protection integrity.
Evaluate potential long-term reliability risks and mitigation.

components.name: Phase Fuse L2
components.clue: Fuse continuity on L2 is open.

components.name: Contactor Coil K1
components.clue: Coil resistance is outside expected range.

components.name: Overload Relay
components.clue: Current setting is lower than motor FLC requirement.

components.name: Auxiliary Hold Contact
components.clue: Contact path is continuous.

repairOptions.label: Set overload relay to motor FLC
Bypass overload relay to keep running

scenarios.debrief: Phase loss, weak coil behavior, and incorrect overload setting combined to cause trip instability. Full coordinated correction restored safe starter performance.

scenarios.title: Signal Conditioning Cabinet Drift
scenarios.brief: A condition-monitoring cabinet is outputting unstable trend data. Recover a clean and trusted signal chain before maintenance decisions are compromised.
preTaskBrief: Define your reference first: identify what 'good' waveform and offset should be.
Prioritise grounding and reference integrity before replacing active parts.
Use comparative reasoning: sensor input, amplifier stage, filtered output.
scenarios.stretchTask: Advanced extension: estimate how noise and offset error could mislead predictive maintenance thresholds.
objectives: Validate reference ground and offset conditions

teaching.vocationalScenario: Learners are tasked with maintaining a monitoring cabinet where poor signal quality risks incorrect service decisions and unnecessary downtime.
lectureSegment: Review op-amp conditioning roles in industrial sensing.
Explain grounding, offset, and gain drift impact on maintenance analytics.
Introduce verification criteria for signal quality handover.
activitySegment: Teams establish expected signal behavior before probing.
Learners compare readings across the signal path and isolate fault origins.
Teams repair, validate waveform quality, and justify maintenance confidence.
pass: Perform basic signal checks and identify at least two suspect points.
Carry out corrective actions with tutor guidance.
Confirm improved signal output after repair.
merit: Diagnose all key faults and explain their impact on measurement quality.
Demonstrate systematic troubleshooting with minimal supervision.
distinction: Restore full signal integrity efficiently and defend diagnosis with strong evidence.
Evaluate system-level consequences of poor signal quality.
Deliver assessor-ready technical report suitable for maintenance planning.

components.name: Reference Ground Lug
components.clue: Ground lug shows loose termination and intermittent continuity.

components.name: Feedback Resistor Rfb
components.clue: Measured resistance is above tolerance by a large margin.

components.name: Op-Amp U2
components.clue: Input offset exceeds expected specification.

components.name: Output Filter Capacitor
components.clue: Capacitance and ESR test within expected bounds.

repairOptions.label: Replace op-amp U2 and recheck offset

scenarios.debrief: Ground reference instability, gain drift, and op-amp offset combined to corrupt cabinet outputs. Correcting all three restored trustworthy conditioning performance.
